text.p: Following are the main stories in the Croatian newspapers on Thursday.
- Government will keep covering deficites of INA oil company as long as state budget permits it, preventing rise of oil-product prices, minister of economy Davor Stern said.
- Proposal of the new law on damages for property confiscated or nationalised since 1945, stipulates maximum return of 3.7 million kuna.
- Stretch of the vital Zagreb - Rijeka highway between Karlovac and Delnice to be opened in November will shorten the route by 30 kilometers.
- Rijeka Riadria bank as of this month resumes extending 15 year loans for buying flats, of up to 100,000 German marks.
- Ministry of tourism offers cheap out of the season holidays for pensioners, covering cost of transport and a half of week's hotel fees.
- Autumn might bring changes in management of troubled hotels along Makarska riviera.
- Identification of 200 bodies in freshly excavated biggest mass grave in Croatia may finish by February, or take as much as another year, forensic expert Davvor Strinovic says.
- Wheat-gate was made up, chairman of the board for state reserves Kresimir Beno accused of speculations with wheat, says.
- British Princess Anne who heads humanitarian organisation Save Children visited port of Split following her tour in Bosnia. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
